newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-MALONE AND JORDAN UNANIMOUS SELECTIONS TO ALL-NBA TEAM.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-MALONE AND JORDAN UNANIMOUS SELECTIONS TO ALL-NBA TEAM.

text.p: NBA Most Valuable Player Karl Malone of the Utah Jazz and Chicago Bulls superstar guard Michael Jordan were unanimous selections to the 1996-97 All-NBA First Team announced on Wednesday.

Malone and Jordan, unanimous choices for the second and fourth times, respectively, received the maximum 115 votes for the First Team from a panel of writers and broadcasters throughout the United States and Canada.
They were joined on the First Team by Houston Rockets centre Hakeem Olajuwon, Detroit Pistons forward Grant Hill and Miami Heat guard Tim Hardaway.

The 115-member panel consisted of 28 national media members and three media members who cover the NBA regularly from each of the league's 29 cities. Media voted for All-NBA First, Second and Third teams by position with points awarded on a 5-3-1 basis.
Malone and Jordan received 575 points each. Olajuwon garnered 514 points, Hill got 483 and Hardaway received 435 points.
Malone averaged 27.4 points, 9.9 rebounds and a career-best 4.5 assists in leading the Jazz to a team-record 64-18 mark this season.
Jordan won his unprecedented ninth scoring title with a 29.7 average this season. He also averaged 5.9 rebounds and 4.3 assists and led the Bulls to an NBA-best mark of 69-13.
This marks the ninth All-NBA First Team selection for Malone and Jordan, the sixth for Olajuwon, and the first for Hardaway and Hill.

Olajuwon averaged 23.2 points and 9.2 rebounds for the Rockets. Hill led the Pistons in scoring (21.4 ppg), rebounding (9.0 rpg) and assists (7.3 apg). Hardaway averaged 20.3 points and 8.6 assists for the Heat, who won a franchise-record 61 games.

The All-NBA Second Team consists of Chicago's Scottie Pippen and Glen Rice of Charlotte at forward, centre Patrick Ewing of the Knicks and guards Gary Payton of Seattle and Mitch Richmond of Sacramento.
The Third Team includes Charlotte's Anthony Mason and Vin Baker of Milwaukee at forward, centre Shaquille O'Neal of the Lakers and guards John Stockton of the Jazz and Penny Hardaway of Orlando.
